claims.statement: Chiang Mai's burning season typically runs from late February through April, with the worst air quality concentrated in March.
During peak burning season, Chiang Mai's PM2.5 and AQI levels can reach unhealthy to hazardous thresholds by international air quality standards.
November through January is generally the cleanest-air stretch of the year in Chiang Mai, and the best window for outdoor training.
Wildcat shifts outdoor session timing and moves technical work under the covered ring on high-AQI days.
claims.allowed_wording: Premiere personne (Meaw), experience directe du camp — aucune source externe requise.
claims.limits: Decrire comme une pratique observee du camp, jamais comme un protocole medical ou une garantie de securite.

claims.statement: Agricultural crop-residue burning across northern Thailand, Laos, and Myanmar, combined with Chiang Mai's valley geography trapping smoke, drives the seasonal spike in air pollution.

People with asthma, heart or lung conditions, pregnant people, young children, and the elderly should take extra precaution and consult a doctor before intense outdoor exercise during high-AQI periods.
claims.limits: Recommandation generale de sante publique, jamais un avis medical individualise.

claims.statement: Training outdoors during burning season poses no health risk.
claims.limits: Ne jamais minimiser le risque sante a des fins commerciales — contredit le disclaimer YMYL obligatoire.
